solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: The old record sex with 25% of aphrodisiacs — "helps one remember what a stiff one was like"

definitions.text: "helps one remember what a stiff one was like"

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is an old format of record
it is a coy word for sex
a quarter of the twelve letters of aphrodisiacs, the first three

explanation.surface: A smutty tale of an old disc and aphrodisiacs, with a quote about a stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: A stiff is slang for a corpse, so the quote is about remembering the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is an inscription on a tombstone commemorating the person buried there.

clue.text: Dick as well as Henry put inside

indicators.note: something put inside is placed within the other word, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: plus means in addition to
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Two men, Dick and Henry, are both being put inside, as if jailed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is slang for the penis, and a phallus is the penis or an image of it.

clue.text: Brown will need skill to be on the up in March

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: art is a skill or craft
Gordon Brown was a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown needs some political skill to climb back in the polls come March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a colour but is the former Prime Minister Gordon Brown, an MP; 'March' is the verb, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk with heavy, steady steps, which is what marching involves.

clue.text: Show by a sullen mistress of French leader

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial show or display
taken as written
dour means stern and sullen

explanation.surface: A show put on by the sulky mistress of a French president.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame de Pompadour was the celebrated royal mistress of King Louis XV of France.

clue.text: State's in a bad way, embracing spending initially — pretend it's something else?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the outer words wrap round a letter

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, plus the 's

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of spending
off means gone bad, as food or a person feeling unwell

explanation.surface: A state in financial trouble starts its spending, then pretends the problem is something else.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something off is to present it falsely as something it is not.

clue.text: In the thick of some cream on goolies

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters within them

parts.note: a run of letters across these three words

explanation.surface: A crude picture of someone smothered in cream on their testicles; goolies is British slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the thick of something means being surrounded by it, in the midst of it.

clue.text: Support for oil painting of Maggie, hatless, after uneasy rest

indicators.note: after means the first piece is placed following the second one in the answer
uneasy suggests restlessness, so the letters of the next word are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: without a hat means the three letters spelling that headgear are taken away

parts.note: Maggie is Margaret Thatcher, the former British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: An oil portrait of Margaret Thatcher bareheaded, painted after a restless sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hatless' reads as Maggie without headgear, but it removes the very word for a hat from inside her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is the wooden frame over which an artist's canvas is pulled tight before painting.

clue.text: Uptight friar left pissed outside entrance to urinal

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the next piece

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for friar, as in Friar Tuck

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of urinal

explanation.surface: A tense friar, left drunk, hangs about outside the gents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb about the friar being abandoned, but it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretful means anxious and agitated, the state of someone who is uptight.

clue.text: (& 21dn.) Barack Obama ends with traumas, juggling a lot of different positions

indicators.note: juggling throws things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order
the ends of the two names are their final letters

parts.note: last letters of Barack and Obama
taken as written

explanation.surface: Barack Obama ends up traumatised by having to juggle many different political positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Positions' looks political, as in policy stances, but means sexual positions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kama Sutra is the ancient Indian treatise on love, famous for describing many sexual positions.

clue.text: PM engineered mob rule on Tyneside?

indicators.note: something engineered is constructed afresh, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister accused of engineering mob rule in Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Melbourne was British Prime Minister in the 1830s, Queen Victoria's first premier.

clue.text: Dead against the end of Labour? Not now!

parts.note: the late so-and-so is someone dead

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A political cry against the death of the Labour Party, then a brush-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Later is what you say to put something off: not at this moment, some time afterwards.

clue.text: Go nuts with a bit of heavy breathing, cheeky!

parts.note: to flip is to lose one's temper or go crazy
a pant is a single short, heavy breath

explanation.surface: Someone loses it while breathing heavily down the phone, and is told off for cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means treating serious matters with disrespectful levity, which is cheeky behaviour.

clue.text: Escape the consequences of budget of fool at heart?

indicators.note: at heart means the letters sit in the interior of the phrase, not at its edges

parts.note: a run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: Asks whether a foolish Chancellor can dodge the fallout from his budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off is to avoid punishment, as a defendant who is acquitted.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Brown's apparent self-image wrecked by favourite howler — pointless sod!

indicators.note: the letters are smashed up and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: a point here is a compass point, and E for east is the one dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: Mockery of a prime minister's grand self-regard after a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown, then UK prime minister, told Parliament in 2008 that 'we not only saved the world' when he meant the banks; the howler is that slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The title a messiah-figure holds, which Brown's slip seemed to claim for himself.

clue.text: David, et al, bonkers — that's confirmed!

indicators.note: bonkers means crazy, so the letters go wild and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: David and his friends are mad, and that's official.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate something is to check and certify that it is correct, so validated means confirmed.

clue.text: Accommodating shag, chain removed from watch — is deceived

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the outer letters make space for another piece

parts.note: a fob is a chain attached to a pocket watch
taken off, as a chain unhooked from a watch
to bed someone is to have sex with them; shag is British slang for this

explanation.surface: A sordid tale of sex, a watch chain taken off, and someone being duped.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fobbed off is to be put off or cheated with an excuse or something inferior.

clue.text: see 28ac.
(& 26dn.) As a careful sunbather pissed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: thoroughly coated in oil, as someone protecting their skin from the sun
second meaning: drunk, as pissed is British slang for being drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally for the sunbather and as slang for the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-oiled is an informal idiom for being drunk, and literally describes skin covered in sun oil.

clue.text: Observer's range of mags (sexy)

parts.note: Private Eye is a magazine, so several such magazines are Eyes
hot means sexually attractive

explanation.surface: A range of sexy magazines, as if from a newspaper's top-shelf collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' tempts as the Sunday newspaper, but it is just someone watching; the magazines are Private Eyes, the setter's own publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshot is the distance within which something can be seen, a watcher's field of vision.

clue.text: Fruity thing, lippy imitation of a fart

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soft red berry
second meaning: the rude noise made by blowing through the lips

explanation.walkthrough: Blowing a raspberry comes from rhyming slang, raspberry tart for fart.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the fruit and the derisive noise made with the tongue and lips.

clue.text: (see 9ac.)
Cry "that hurt end of thingy!", being something of a coward?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'being somewhat cowardly'

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
ow is the exclamation when something hurts

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of thingy

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks that their thingy hurts, revealing themselves as a bit of a wimp.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow means cowardly, and the -y ending softens it to 'somewhat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowy means somewhat yellow, and yellow is an informal word for cowardly.

clue.text: Sailor who's experienced a dose screwed good

indicators.note: screwed means twisted, so the letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A sailor who caught a dose, meaning venereal disease, after a good screw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old, experienced sailor, a veteran of long voyages.

clue.text: Member's area — Right gatecrashing to gain access

indicators.note: a gatecrasher forces their way into a party, so one letter forces its way into a phrase

parts.note: to go in is to enter
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A members' area of a club where a right-winger crashes the gate to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club member, but here it is the male member.
explanation.definitionFit: The groin is the region where the legs meet the body, where the penis is located.

clue.text: see 14ac.
see 18ac.
Awkward situation: dish snuggled up to a Tory (not right wing)

indicators.note: the dish sits right up against what follows

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew, a dish

indicators.note: not means the named letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written
the right-hand wing of the word, its end letters

explanation.surface: A satirical scene of a stew cosying up to a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a slow-cooked British stew; Tory loses its right-hand end to leave TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an issue so controversial that nobody wants to handle it.

clue.text: (& 17 ac.) Shit raked over in Hello, possibly? It's a get-out

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the rearranged letters
possibly says the letters of Hello may be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: raked over suggests turning the stuff back on itself, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: poo is a slang word for excrement

explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a celebrity magazine; 'possibly' scrambles its title, and the reversed slang word sits inside, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in rules that lets someone escape an obligation, an escape route.

clue.text: Maybe co-ed gives "sex machine" brief amusement?

parts.note: a stud is a sexually prolific man

indicators.note: the word is cut short to its first three letters

parts.note: amusement is entertainment

explanation.surface: A college girl entertains a would-be lothario for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-ed is a female student at a mixed college, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Dicky died, say, getting screwed — not the best of times

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, and off means much the same
d is the abbreviation for died

indicators.note: screwed means twisted, so these letters are twisted into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Dicky died after a screw, which hardly sounds like a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: Off days are days when one performs below one's usual standard.
